title: Bitfilters
subtitle: Compact membership checks for large sets.
intro: Aggregate hashed keys into a compact BLOB, then probe it to reject definite nonmembers. Use an exact check for candidates that survive the filter.

reference.name: xor8_filter(hash)
reference.description: Aggregate UBIGINT hashes into a static XOR filter.

reference.name: xor8_filter_contains(filter, hash)
reference.description: Return whether a key might be in the set.

reference.name: xor16_filter / xor16_filter_contains
reference.description: Use wider fingerprints for fewer false positives.

reference.name: binary_fuse8_filter / binary_fuse16_filter
reference.description: Alternative static filters with matching _contains probes.

reference.name: quotient_filter(q, r, hash)
reference.description: Build a quotient filter; q and r control capacity and precision.

reference.name: quotient_filter_contains(filter, hash)
reference.description: Probe a quotient filter with the same hash representation.

notes.title: A positive is only a candidate
notes.body: Keep an exact join or membership predicate after probing. False positives are expected; correctly built filters retain inserted keys.

notes.title: Hash consistently
notes.body: Use the same function, seed and SQL input type when building and probing. Treat DuckDB hash() as version-dependent; persist its version or choose an explicit hash algorithm.

examples.title: Build once
examples.caption: Constructors aggregate rows; the result is a BLOB you can persist.

examples.title: Probe candidates
examples.caption: Inserted keys return true. An unseen key can also return true.

examples.title: Confirm the match
examples.sql:
SELECT i
FROM known_filter, range(995, 1005) AS t(i)
WHERE xor8_filter_contains(f, hash(i))
  AND i IN (SELECT range FROM range(1000));
examples.caption: The final exact predicate returns only IDs 995 through 999.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT bool_and(xor8_filter_contains(f,hash(i))) FROM known_filter,range(1000)t(i)) THEN true ELSE error('false negative') END;
